cards.text: Letter time, friend. The writer of Hebrews has been telling his "holy brothers" (Hebrews 3:1) that Christ is the mediator of a new covenant (Hebrews 9:15). Now he turns to the sacrifices offered under the law, and he starts with a picture: the law is only a shadow.

cards.question: The writer of Hebrews calls the law only a shadow. A shadow of what?

cards.text: A shadow, "not the realities themselves." I once tried to grab a cookie's shadow off my counter with my mustache, and friend, I grabbed that counter FIVE times before I let it go.

cards.question: Under the law, the same sacrifices are offered year after year. The writer says those sacrifices can make the worshipers perfect.
If those sacrifices could make worshipers perfect, what does the writer say would have happened to the offerings?

cards.text: If those sacrifices really worked, the worshipers would have been cleansed for good and would no longer have felt the guilt of their sins. Friend, if the plumber actually fixes the leak, you do NOT call him back every single year.

cards.question: But the sacrifices keep coming. The writer says those sacrifices are an annual ___ of sins.

cards.text: Here's why: "it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins." So it's like a phone alert that pops up every year yelling YOUR BILL IS DUE, and that alert has never once paid the bill.
Big moment, friend, so I'm shutting off every mixer in the bakery. The writer says that when Christ came into the world, He spoke to God in words from Psalm 40.

cards.question: When Christ came into the world, what did He tell God about sacrifice and offering?
Christ goes on, still speaking to God. He says God prepared a ___ for Him.

cards.text: Then Christ says, "Here I am…" and that it is written about Him in the scroll. Friend, I'm leaning in so far my gold base is tipping.

cards.question: Christ says it is written about Him in the scroll. What does He say He has come to do?

cards.text: Then the writer replays those words FRAME by FRAME, like a coach with game film. He lists the sacrifices and offerings again and says God didn't delight in them.

cards.question: The writer adds a note about those sacrifices and offerings: they are offered according to the law.

cards.text: Then the writer says, "He takes away the first to establish the second." Let that one sit a second, friend.
Here's the payoff, friend, and I'm so excited I just stamped my own apron. By that will, the writer says, we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ.

cards.question: The old sacrifices came year after year. But the body of Jesus Christ was sacrificed ___, and through it we have been sanctified.

cards.text: Day after day, every priest stands to minister. Again and again, the SAME sacrifices, and the writer says they can never take away sins.

cards.question: Jesus, this Priest, offered one sacrifice for sins for all time. What did He do after that?

answers.text: He sat down at God's right hand
He went back into the temple
He went out into the wilderness

cards.question: Since that time, Jesus waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet.
By a single offering, Jesus has made ___ for all time those who are being sanctified.

cards.text: Then the writer says the Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First, in words from Jeremiah 31, the Lord declares a covenant He will make with them after those days.

cards.question: In this covenant, where does the Lord say He will put His laws?
In this covenant, the Lord says He will remember their sins and lawless acts every year.
Where sins have been forgiven, what does the writer say is no longer needed?
